title: Checkboxes, Radios & Selects 📋
description: Make multi‑option inputs clear, groupable, and keyboard‑navigable using native HTML and ARIA.

slides.title: The Power of Native Widgets 💪
slides.content:
Checkboxes, radio buttons, and selects are natively keyboard‑accessible. Avoid recreating them from scratch unless absolutely necessary.

* `<input type="checkbox">` – toggles on/off, Space key.
* `<input type="radio">` – one option in a group, arrow keys navigate.
* `<select>` – dropdown list, arrow keys, type‑ahead.

Styling limitations are not a good enough reason to reinvent them with divs.

quizData.question: Which key toggles a native checkbox?
quizData.explanation: Space checks/unchecks a checkbox; Enter typically submits the surrounding form.

slides.title: Radio Groups: The Proper Way 📻
slides.content:
Radio buttons with the same `name` attribute form a group. Only one can be selected.

* Wrap them in a `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`.
* Arrow keys cycle through options.
* Tab moves focus to the group (to the selected radio) and then Tab again leaves the group.

This built‑in keyboard behaviour is excellent.

slides.title: Accessible Radio Group
slides.codeSnippet:
<fieldset>
  <legend>Shipping method</legend>
  <input type="radio" id="standard" name="shipping" value="standard" checked>
  <label for="standard">Standard (free)</label>
  <input type="radio" id="express" name="shipping" value="express">
  <label for="express">Express ($5)</label>
</fieldset>

quizData.question: What defines which radio buttons belong to the same group?
quizData.explanation: The `name` attribute groups radios; the browser enforces mutual exclusivity.

slides.title: Custom Checkboxes & Radios (If You Must) 🎨

quizData.question: What is the safest way to create a visually custom checkbox?

options.text: Hide the native checkbox and style its label using CSS
Use JavaScript to toggle a hidden input

quizData.explanation: Keeping the native input preserves keyboard, focus, and screen reader support.

slides.title: Selects & Multi‑selects 📜
slides.content:
Native `<select>` (and `<select multiple>`) are accessible but limited in styling.

* Always provide a visible `<label>`.
* Use `<optgroup>` for grouping options – screen readers announce the group label.
* Avoid `<option>` without a value – use a prompt like `<option value="">-- Choose --</option>`.

If you need a custom select, build a combobox (next lesson).

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Don't use `aria-selected` on native `<option>`
Native selects manage their own state. ARIA selection attributes can conflict.
